villages.name: San Benedetto
villages.description: A hamlet gathered under the walls of a Benedictine priory. The monks keep bees, bake the altar breads and pour the candles for half the diocese.
gossip: The brothers sing the Office seven times a day. Some travellers stop only to hear it.
Prior Odo says a pilgrim never leaves San Benedetto without bread in his pack.

villages.name: Sant'Agnese
villages.description: Shepherds' cottages around a chapel of St Agnes. On her feast the lambs are blessed, and their wool is spun for the pallia of the bishops.
gossip: Every spring the best lamb of the flock goes to the Cathedral of the Lamp.
The shepherds say wolves will not cross the chapel's boundary stones.

villages.name: San Isidro
villages.description: A farming hamlet named for St Isidore the labourer. Its wheat fields run right up to the feet of the Spine.
gossip: They say St Isidore's angels plough the fields while the farmers are at Mass.
Good seed corn is kept here in the church loft, blessed on Rogation Days.

villages.name: Sant'Ambrogio
villages.description: Hives line every garden wall of this hamlet of St Ambrose, patron of beekeepers. Its honey is sweet and its wax burns clean.
gossip: Old Brother Ivo talks to the bees each morning, and tells them every death and every wedding.
Their mead is so good that even the scholars of Porticus send for it.

villages.name: San Rocco
villages.description: A hospice of St Roch on the pilgrims' road, with a dog carved over its gate. The sick are nursed here for nothing.
gossip: The hospitallers ask no one his faith before they dress his wounds.
A faithful dog brought St Roch his bread. The hamlet dogs are fed first at every feast.

villages.name: Gallows Cross
villages.description: Four roads meet under an old gibbet. The Pact holds its markets here at midnight, and nobody asks where the goods came from.
gossip: Do not bargain after the third bell. What is sold then cannot be bought back.
The rope on the gibbet is never taken down. They say it is waiting for someone.

villages.name: Crowsfoot
villages.description: A huddle of black timber houses where three tracks split like a crow's claw. Woodcutters live here, and stranger folk.
gossip: The woodcutters cut only by moonlight. They say the trees bleed otherwise.
A traveller who whistles on the crow's road is never seen again. Keep quiet.

villages.name: Widow's Turning
villages.description: Shuttered houses at a bend of the dead wood, where a widow once sold her husband's soul for a purse of gold. Tar pits smoke behind them.
gossip: The tar pits never cool. Some say the fire comes from below.
The widow still keeps the inn, they say, and she has not aged a day.

villages.name: Hangman's Fork
villages.description: A coal-pit hamlet under the Barrow Fells, ringed with slag heaps and gallows. The colliers pay their tithe to the Black Pact.
gossip: Down in the deep seams the colliers hear knocking. They knock back, three times, for luck.
The hangman here is also the mayor, and the priest, and the judge.

villages.name: Montevino
villages.description: A hill town of terraced vines and painted shutters. Every cellar door stands open, and every cellar has a song.
gossip: The harvest dance lasts three nights. Whoever falls asleep first pays for the fourth.
Old Dom Ferrante swears his red is older than the Church. He is lying, but pour him another.

villages.name: Vigna Rossa
villages.description: Red vines to the horizon and a press house as big as a cathedral. The grape treaders work to fiddles and drums.
gossip: Their wine is so dark it stains the moon, the treaders say.
A merchant from Vinemere comes every week to taste the casks. He leaves on a cart, never on foot.

villages.name: Malvasia
villages.description: A sun-baked village under the Vintner's Ridge, famous for its sweet white wine and its spice merchants from over the sea.
gossip: Ships unload pepper and cinnamon at the cove below, and nobody pays the toll.
Drink the Malvasia slowly. It is sweet going down and bitter in the morning.

villages.name: Mascarino
villages.description: A village of mask makers and ribbon weavers. Half its houses are workshops, and the other half are taverns.
gossip: Nobody in Mascarino shows his face on a feast night. Not even to his wife.
The mask makers say every face they carve is somebody's. Pray it is not yours.

villages.name: Dafni
villages.description: A village of laurel groves and white walls. Its wreaths crown the victors of the games at Porticus.
gossip: The elders argue in the square every evening. Nobody wins, but everybody enjoys it.
A laurel leaf under the pillow brings clear dreams, the village women say.

villages.name: Elaia
villages.description: Silver olive terraces above the cold sea. The presses of Elaia have run since before the philosophers had names.
gossip: Old Nikandros keeps an olive tree he says was planted by Zeno himself.
The best oil is pressed cold, and sold only to those who ask politely.

villages.name: Libanos
villages.description: A quiet village of resin gatherers. Incense from its trees burns in the temples of the Stoa, and in the Church's censers too.
gossip: The resin weeps from the bark like tears. They gather it at dawn, in silence.
A priest from Santa Lucerna comes each Lent to buy incense. He and the elders talk until midnight.

villages.name: Melissai
villages.description: Beehives of woven straw on every rooftop. The village is named for the bees, which the scholars say keep a perfect republic.
gossip: Plato would have liked our bees, the keepers say: every one knows its place.
Thyme honey from Melissai is the only sweet the Stoics allow themselves.

villages.name: Hollin Dell
villages.description: Round houses in a dell of holly and oak. The folk here keep wild bees in hollow trunks and brew the old mead.
gossip: Never cut holly in Hollin Dell. The Holly King remembers.
Our bees knew the forest before the first king was crowned.

villages.name: Ashgrove
villages.description: Woodcutters and charcoal burners among tall ash trees. They take only fallen wood, and leave an offering for each branch.
gossip: The great ash at the heart of the grove has never been touched by an axe.
Charcoal from Ashgrove burns hotter than any coal from the pits.

villages.name: Mossbrook
villages.description: A sheepfold village beside a mossy brook. Its lambs graze on wild thyme, and the shepherds play pipes at dusk.
gossip: Our fattened lambs fetch double at the feasts of Vinemere.
The brook speaks if you listen long enough. Mostly it speaks of rain.

villages.name: Thornwick
villages.description: A hedged village at the edge of the Barrow Fells. Bay and laurel grow in its sheltered gardens, out of the wind.
gossip: The barrows on the fells are older than Elderholt. Do not sleep on them.
Thornwick hedges are planted with thorn so no spirit can wander in.

villages.name: Rowan Hollow
villages.description: A hidden hamlet deep in the oak wood, under red rowan berries. Its mead halls are older than any road.
gossip: Rowan wood over the door keeps the evil eye away.
The mead of Rowan Hollow is brewed with nine herbs. Nobody outside knows which nine.

villages.name: Sixmills
villages.description: Six great waterwheels turn along the race, grinding grain for Cogspire day and night. The miller's guild rings a bell at every shift.
gossip: The sixth mill has not stopped in forty years. The guild has a wager on it.
Flour from Sixmills is so fine the bakers of Cogspire weigh it by the ounce.

villages.name: Slagford
villages.description: A smithing town at a ford choked with slag. The forges cast pots, cauldrons and the iron of half the bridges in the land.
gossip: The ironmasters test every cauldron by ringing it. A dull note goes back into the furnace.
When the wind is from the west, Slagford smells of hot iron for a mile.

villages.name: Coalpit Row
villages.description: Terraced cottages over the coal seams. The winding gear clanks all day, and the colliers come up black at sunset.
gossip: The guild bought the deep seam from Ashenmouth. Nobody asks what was paid.
A collier's lamp that burns blue means firedamp. Run.

villages.name: Furnace End
villages.description: The last stop on the foundry road: oil works and boiling vats where the guild renders the oils that keep the engines turning.
gossip: The overseer says one day the engines will run without oil. He has said it for twenty years.
Do not light a pipe within a hundred paces of the vats.

villages.name: Grindwell
villages.description: A windmill town on the shoulder of the Spine. Its sails grind wheat in summer and sugar cane brought up from the coast in winter.
gossip: When the sails stop, the whole town comes out to look. It means the wind has changed.
The miller's daughter can tell the weather by the creak of the cogs.
